stem: Which of the following represents the correct north to south sequence of following four islands of Japan?
expl: The correct sequence of the four islands of Japan in a north to south direction is as follows–Hokkaido–Honshu–Shikoku– Kyushu. Honshu is the largest and most populous island of Japan. The island separates the sea of Japan from the North Pacific Ocean. Hokkaido–is the second largest island of Japan. The Tsugaru Strait separates Hokkaido from Honshu. One of Japan's most active volcanoes, Mt. Aso is on Kyushu Island.

stem: Where are the Balearic islands located ?

stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the Islands of Indonesia from West to East?
expl: • The correct sequence of the Islands of Indonesia from West to East is - Sumatra, Java, Bali and Lombok. • Indonesia's islands can be grouped into the Greater Sunda Islands of Sumatra (Sumatera), Java (Jawa), the southern extent of Borneo (Kalimantan), and Celebes (Sulawesi); the Lesser Sunda Islands (Nusa Tenggara) of Bali and a chain of islands that runs eastward through Timor; the Moluccas (Maluku) between Celebes and the island of New Guinea; and the western extent of New Guinea (generally known as Papua). • The capital, Jakarta, is located near the northwestern coast of Java.

stem: Which of the following Islands is NOT located in the Caribbean Sea?
expl: • The Caribbean Islands is a massive archipelago located in the Caribbean Sea that can be subdivided into a few different regions: the Lucayan Archipelago, the Greater Antilles, the Lesser Antilles and the ABC Islands. • There are 13 sovereign states and 17 dependent territories in the Caribbean, and the predominant languages are English, Spanish,French, Dutch and Antillean Creole. Major islands include - Anguilla, Antigua, British Virgin Islands, Grenada, Montserrat, Saint Martin, etc. • Madeira Islands, is an archipelago of volcanic origin in the North Atlantic Ocean, belonging to Portugal. It comprises two inhabited islands, Madeira and Porto Santo, and two uninhabited groups, the Desertas and the Selvagens.
